notes: Matched on same passage and rule; A's two scale units (scale name and No AI row) were matched to B's single scale unit (scale name matched, No AI row counted only_A). Main disagreements: (1) policy_type between a misconduct-classification type (P36) and a more specific type, resolved by which element the sentence's condition names: P19 for AI completing assigned work, P28 for uncredited AI work; (2) P77 vs P56 for the opening line (P77, existing policy); P95 vs P56 for the ethical-use expectation (P95, neutral); P26 vs P24 for the document-and-cite item (P24, nothing says logs are submitted); P50 vs P49 for confidential or copyrighted information (P50, no upload mentioned); P04 vs P78 for the faculty-permission checklist item (P04). (3) Phase: when-misuse vs during-work for definitional misconduct and checklist sentences, decided by whether the sentence describes an act at work time or a classification. (4) Modality and policy for the MLA and APA lines: set to informs with policy that does not say students must use the format. (5) Actor all vs student for the authorization definition: student. Both only-A units (No AI row, checklist intro) and the only-B unit (cheating definition) are real policy statements and were kept. Both fit_notes sets were merged and no new types were proposed.
